Honda Says It Brings Enhanced Value Across the CR-V and ZR-V Ranges With a Reduced Pricing Structure
6 photos
Photo: Honda
The Japanese automaker Honda is revealing new prices, effective November 2, for the CR-V and ZR-V compact crossover SUVs in the United Kingdom, one of their most important markets across the Old Continent.
The company has been pretty busy lately celebrating the milestone of 500 Formula One races, marked at the recently concluded 2026 United States Grand Prix, but also showcasing numerous mobility innovations at the Japan Mobility Show Bizweek and CEATEC 2026. As for the United Kingdom, the market is also well stocked, as it recently got the upgraded Honda Civic e:HEV with the new Honda S+ Shift feature and an enhanced Sport grade.
There was also the tiny Honda Super-N, which won the Fun Car of the Year award at the News UK Motor Awards 2026, or the newly announced Prelude 2027 Limited Edition featuring the new and exclusive Premium Crystal Garnet Metallic exterior paint and a luxurious Bordeaux interior available across Europe this autumn, among others.
Now, though, it’s time to focus on SUVs in the United Kingdom , where Honda is introducing a new pricing structure for the compact ZR-V and the slightly larger CR-V crossovers, “further reinforcing Honda's commitment to delivering exceptional value alongside advanced hybrid technology, premium comfort and everyday practicality.”
The new OTR (on-the-road) pricing sees the Honda ZR-V e:HEV start from £35,215 (a little over $47k at the current exchange rate) for the Elegance trim, while the Sport and Advance are £37,455 ($50k) and £39,585 ($53k), respectively. Previously, the three models kicked off at £36,525; £38,765; and £40,895, respectively.
Meanwhile, the Honda CR-V is available both as a hybrid and as a plug-in hybrid variant. The CR-V e:HEV has two grades: Elegance from £43,995 ($59k) and Advance from £46,995 ($63k), while the CR-V e:PHEV has Elegance and Advance Tech from £44,995 ($60k) and £47,995 (over $64k), respectively. Prior to the new pricing changes, they were £48,075 and £51,520 for the e:HEV, or at least £47,795 for the cheapest e:PHEV.
The Honda ZR-V e:HEV has a 2.0-liter full hybrid powertrain with 184 combined ps or 181 hp, combining “sporty design, advanced hybrid technology and everyday practicality in a sophisticated SUV package.” It lands between the HR-V and the CR-V, with the latter being Honda's largest SUV in Europe. The CR-V is available with both e:HEV full hybrid and e:PHEV plug-in hybrid powertrains, offering up to 596 miles (WLTP) of total range and an EV-only range of up to 50 miles in e:PHEV form.
“Honda is committed to delivering great value alongside the quality, technology and reliability customers expect from the brand. This new pricing structure strengthens the appeal of both the CR-V and ZR-V, making our electrified SUVs an even more compelling choice for customers,” explains Michael Doyle, Head of Automobile at Honda Motor Europe (UK).
